key_insight: A self-supervised functional autoencoder learns a reusable, task-agnostic latent space, separating function representation from neural operator training.
engineering_relevance: For solid-mechanics surrogates, frozen representations can reduce operator-training memory and time while supporting fields sampled on arbitrary point clouds.
method: Pre-train a functional autoencoder on analytic functions synthesized without solvers or labels.
Freeze translation-, dilation-, and amplitude-equivariant representation maps, then train operators on cached embeddings.
Run predictions and rollouts in latent space, with chunked decoding for large fields.
evidence_signal: Across 28 tasks spanning solid mechanics, fluids, acoustics, Helmholtz, and Poisson equations, the abstract reports accuracy that can exceed state-of-the-art end-to-end models, up to an order-of-magnitude higher throughput, and inference on over half a billion points using one consumer-grade GPU.
watch_item: For engineering deployment, validate transfer accuracy and physical fidelity on the intended geometries, boundary conditions, and material regimes; aggregate benchmarks do not guarantee reliability for every mechanics problem.
paper_title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
